cita: Wei et al. (2026). FadeMem: Biologically-Inspired Forgetting for Efficient Agent Memory.
problema: LLM agents lack selective forgetting: they either drop everything at context boundaries (catastrophic loss) or keep everything and drown in irrelevant clutter as memory scales, unlike human memory's graded decay.
mecanismo: Dual-layer memory (LML/SML) where an importance score (relevance+decayed access frequency+recency) governs layer assignment with hysteresis; each memory decays via a differential exponential curve (sub-linear in LML, super-linear in SML) and is reinforced on access; new memories are LLM-classified against similar ones (compatible/contradictory/subsumes/subsumed) and related clusters are LLM-fused into consolidated memories.
evaluacion: Evaluated on Multi-Session Chat, LoCoMo and a synthetic 30-day LTI-Bench (10,780 interaction sequences) against Fixed-window/LangChain/Mem0/MemGPT baselines using SRR, RP@K, TCS, F1, FCR; ablation on LoCoMo removes dual-layer, fusion, and conflict-resolution components.
numeros_clave: 82.1% critical-fact retention at only 55.0% storage vs 100% for baselines (LTI-Bench, Table1); LoCoMo multi-hop F1=29.43 (SRR=0.45) vs Mem0 28.37/MemGPT 9.46 (Table3); ablation: removing the dual-layer drops multi-hop F1 29.43->19.45 (-33.9%), removing fusion ->13.63 (-53.7%).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Adaptive decay + LLM-guided fusion (Sec 2.4) is a concrete promote/demote-by-importance mechanism MF could adapt for gotcha->recipe promotion (Table1: 82.1% critical retention at 55% storage).
Measured 45% storage reduction (SRR=0.45, Table3) with F1 gains over baselines confirms pruning/decay is a real cost lever, supporting MF's context-economy stance.
The four-way conflict classification with age-weighted suppression of stale info (Eq.10, Sec2.3) is a reusable staleness-handling mechanism for MF's TIER-DOCS.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (LTI-Bench retention/storage) and Table3+Fig.2 (LoCoMo, ablation deltas); arXiv preprint, evaluation judged via GPT-4o-mini, single-institution.

cita: Li et al. (2026). BMAM: Brain-inspired Multi-Agent Memory Framework.
problema: Agents operating over long horizons suffer 'soul erosion': degradation of temporal coherence, factual consistency, and identity/preference retention, because memory is a single unstructured RAG store instead of functionally specialized subsystems.
mecanismo: Coordinator-centered multi-agent architecture decomposing memory into episodic (timeline-indexed StoryArc), semantic (consolidated knowledge graph), salience-aware, and prefrontal control subsystems; hybrid retrieval fuses lexical/dense/graph/temporal signals via reciprocal rank fusion (Eq.3); background reconsolidation updates fact confidence via an exponential moving average (Eq.4) and prunes low-value episodes.
evaluacion: Evaluated on LoCoMo, LongMemEval, PersonaMem and PrefEval against 7 baselines (MemOS re-run for fairness, Mem0, MIRIX, Zep, Memobase, Supermemory, MemU); brain-region ablation on a LoCoMo subset removes each subsystem in turn.
numeros_clave: 78.45% accuracy on LoCoMo (vs MemOS 75.80%, Fig.3) and 67.60% on LongMemEval (Table3); ablation (Fig.4): removing hippocampus-inspired episodic memory drops accuracy 24.62% (largest single effect); removing the Temporal Lobe module drops temporal-query accuracy 12.3%.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Ablation (Fig.4) shows episodic-memory removal causes the largest accuracy drop (-24.62%), empirically confirming a dedicated consolidation subsystem (not flat RAG) is load-bearing for long-horizon coherence.

The 'soul erosion' formalization (Eq.1-2: temporal/semantic/identity decay of a soulfulness score) is a reusable diagnostic frame MF could adopt to name and measure staleness/drift in its docs-memory.
BMAM's unified substrate spans KV+vector+graph rather than one store per fact (Sec3), relevant context for MF's single-source-per-fact debate but no seam-cost measurement is reported.

notes: Numbers from Table2/Fig.3 (LoCoMo/LongMemEval per-category) and Fig.4 (brain-region ablation); paper re-runs the strongest baseline (MemOS) itself for a fair comparison (Sec4.1), single-benchmark family.

cita: Hu et al. (2026). Beyond RAG for Agent Memory: Retrieval by Decoupling and Aggregation.
problema: Flat top-k similarity retrieval over agent memory (a bounded, highly correlated interaction stream) returns redundant near-duplicate context, while summary-centric hierarchies blur the fine distinguishing details (small updates/constraints) that decide the answer.
mecanismo: 'Decoupling before aggregation': raw messages are segmented into local events, decoupled into atomic reusable memory components (facts/updates/attributes), then aggregated into revisable groups via a sparsity+semantic-faithfulness objective (Eq.1-3) with incremental split/merge maintenance; retrieval proceeds top-down: Stage I greedily selects a complementary group/component backbone by coverage-weighted relevance (Eq.4), Stage II expands to segments/messages only while marginal predictive-uncertainty reduction stays positive (Eq.5).
evaluacion: LoCoMo and PerLTQA across three backbone LLMs (Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B, GPT-5-nano) vs 6 baselines (Full Memory, Naive RAG, LightMem, Nemori, A-Mem, MemoryOS), reporting BLEU/F1/ROUGE-L and tokens/query; ablations on retrieval stages, group-size bound, and dynamic restructuring (reassignment ratio).
numeros_clave: On LoCoMo with Qwen3-8B, avg BLEU/F1 improves from 31.44/40.88 (Nemori) to 34.48/43.98 while tokens/query drop 7755->4711 (Table1); disabling split/merge restructuring drops avg F1 43.98->38.59 at 0% reassignment vs 44.91% reassignment in the full system (Fig.4).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The revisable component-to-group hierarchy with measured split/merge as memory evolves (Sec3.1, Fig.4: 44.91% reassignment improves F1) is a concrete derived-cache pattern MF's TIER-INDICE could adopt instead of a frozen index.

Table1/2 show simultaneously better answer quality AND lower tokens/query than flat RAG or compression baselines, confirming MF's premise that structuring memory (not truncating context) is the real cost lever.

Stage-II uncertainty-driven expansion (include a segment only if it reduces reader predictive entropy, Eq.5) is a measured-retrieval stopping criterion MF could reuse to decide when to expand from index to full docs.

notes: Numbers from Table1 (LoCoMo, Qwen3-8B row) and Sec5.2 Fig.4 (retroactive-restructuring ablation); PerLTQA Table2 corroborates cross-dataset; arXiv preprint (v4), not yet venue-published.

cita: Ma et al. (2026). CAST: Character-and-Scene Episodic Memory for Agents.
problema: Existing agent memory (key-value, vector, graph) treats experience as flat facts and struggles to represent/retrieve coherent EVENTS (who/when/where), so a distinguishing quote or detail can be lost even when related facts are stored.
mecanismo: Dialogue turns become 'views' (speaker/time/place/text/participants), aggregated by 3D closeness in time/place/topic into 'scenes'; scenes attach to role-labeled (main/supporting) character profiles forming episodic memory, complemented by a HippoRAG2-style semantic graph (OpenIE triples); retrieval fuses semantic-graph/DPR results with episodic scene search, promoting entries found in both to the front.
evaluacion: LOCOMO (single/multi/temporal/open subsets) and epbench (default/scifi/news) against RAG, HippoRAG, Zep, Mem0, LangMem baselines; F1 and LLM-as-Judge metrics averaged over 5 runs; parameter ablations vary window size w and scene-clustering thresholds.
numeros_clave: On locomo_open, CAST reaches F1=62.02/J=81.21 vs naive RAG 36.87/56.60 (+25.15 F1/+24.61 J) and beats the best baseline Zep (48.78/72.89) by +13.24 F1/+8.32 J (Table1); averaged across all datasets/baselines, +8.11% F1 and +10.21% J.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Character profiles as a narrative, typed index over scenes (Sec3.1, 'what happened to whom/when/where') is a concrete pattern for organizing docs-as-narrative-truth rather than flat facts, matching MF's TIER-DOCS motivation.

Measured gains concentrated on locomo_open/time where structured episodic retrieval beats flat vector/graph search (Table1) confirms retrieval quality is representation-dependent, supporting a measured-retrieval (G-M2) stance for episodic recall.

CAST fuses two independently indexed stores (semantic graph + episodic scene index, Sec3.2) rather than one source of truth, relevant to MF's single-source-per-fact debate, but no seam-consistency-failure data is reported.

notes: Table1 gives the F1/J deltas per dataset/baseline; parameter sensitivity in Sec4.3.1/Fig.4 continues past the read excerpt but the headline gains are confirmed; anonymized code repo, arXiv preprint.

cita: Shu et al. (2026). REMem: Reasoning with Episodic Memory in Language Agents.
problema: Language-agent memory is mainly semantic and RAG-style, overlooking episodicity and explicit event modeling, so agents cannot reliably recollect situational context (time/place/participants) nor perform multi-step reasoning across linked events.
mecanismo: Two-phase framework: indexing builds a hybrid memory graph of time-aware gists (concise event summaries with resolved timestamps) and time-scoped facts (subject,predicate,object triples with Wikidata-style temporal qualifiers), linked by synonymy edges; agentic inference runs a ReAct-style agent with curated tools (semantic/lexical retrieve, find_gist_contexts, find_entity_contexts with temporal filters, output_answer) that iteratively explores the graph instead of one-shot matching.
evaluacion: Evaluated on LoCoMo, REALTALK (episodic recollection) and Complex-TR, Test of Time (episodic reasoning) against embedding baselines (Qwen3/NV-Embed), Mem0, Graphiti, HippoRAG2, and prompt-based TISER; ablates gists vs facts, synonymy edges, and each retrieval tool.
numeros_clave: REMem-I reaches LLM-J=83.3/EM=90.6 on Complex-TR/Test-of-Time vs HippoRAG2 78.2/66.9 (Table4), a 3.4% and 13.4% absolute improvement over SOTA on recollection/reasoning respectively; ablation: removing gists drops LoCoMo LLM-J 76.2->48.9 (Table5); refusal F1 on unanswerable LoCoMo questions is 64.0% vs Mem0 13.5% (Table6).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Table3/4 measure that iterative agentic multi-hop retrieval over a structured graph (REMem-I) beats single embedding-based retrieval (REMem-S, LLM-J +7.0/EM +20.6 on Complex-TR, Sec5.2) and beats large embedding models outright — direct evidence against a grep/embedding-is-enough default per ADR-019.

Preserving contradictory gists/facts over time rather than overwriting (Sec3.1) plus a measured refusal mechanism (Table6, F1=64.0%) is a concrete pattern for MF's staleness/negative-knowledge handling.
Full-Context uses ~26k input tokens/query on LoCoMo while REMem-I/S use only 9k/0.9k with comparable or better quality (Sec5.1), confirming structured retrieval as a cost lever MF already assumes.

notes: Numbers from Table3/4 (recollection/reasoning) and Table5/6 (ablation, refusal); ICLR 2026 accepted paper, code released (Sec1 footnote), strongest evidence base in this batch.

cita: Tilak (2026). Continuous Memory Consolidation Without Retraining: Solving the Edge Bloat Problem Through Computational Sleep.
problema: Continuously learning knowledge-graph agents accumulate edges every cycle without a removal mechanism ('edge bloat'), degrading query quality as noise overwhelms signal over thousands of learning cycles.
mecanismo: A multi-phase 'computational sleep' consolidation run at intervals: priority-based replay reinforces significant nodes, structural hub reinforcement protects high-degree core concepts, Hebbian associative strengthening boosts co-activated concepts, offline discovery runs forward causal simulation, pattern compression abstracts instances into hierarchies, and controlled pruning removes weak edges under a zero-node-deletion policy.
evaluacion: Single-agent case study on a developmental knowledge-graph agent (4,400+ learning cycles): before/after edge-creation-rate comparison per subsystem, and a 500-cycle stability comparison (consolidated vs unconsolidated graph growth) with edge-weight and reasoning-confidence quality metrics; no external benchmark or baseline system.
numeros_clave: Edge creation rate reduced 195->42 per cycle (78% reduction, Table1); over 500 cycles graph size stabilizes at ~8,200 edges vs unbounded growth to ~23,400 without consolidation; mean edge weight rises 0.18->0.34 and reasoning-chain confidence 0.31->0.47.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The explicit sleep-phase pipeline (replay->hub-reinforcement->pattern-compression->pruning, Sec2) with a measured 78% edge-growth reduction (Table1) is a candidate design MF could mine for its own gotcha-to-recipe promotion/pruning cycle.
Stable ~8,200-edge graph vs unbounded ~23,400-edge growth over 500 cycles (Sec3.2) confirms that periodic consolidation, not accumulation, is required to bound long-run memory cost.

The zero-node-deletion / edge-only-pruning policy (Sec4) implicitly treats concepts as permanent while only weak associative edges are forgotten, tangential to but not the same as MF's negative-knowledge (re-derivation-over-recall) idea.

notes: Self-published single-author technical report (no peer venue, 'proprietary phases' undisclosed in Sec2), all numbers are from one internal developmental agent with no external baseline — RECONSIDERAR (weak evidentiary rigor for this corpus's bar).
